instructions.task: This line opens with When. Does it start a branch, or is it guidance?

criteria.branch: A branch: its condition picks out some runs, and those runs do work the others don't, such as a different action, destination or result.
criteria.guidance: Guidance: the When clause names the moment in every run at which an action happens, or frames a rule that holds whenever its activity does, so no run is sent down a different path.

instructions.task: Read the branch; the step is the heading of the numbered step it sits in, empty when it sits in none. Which part does the branch leave out?

criteria.none: It names a condition an agent can observe in the work (a file, a result, a state, a request, a diff) and the different work that condition causes. Observable conditions include the kind of work in hand, a piece of information the next call needs and the agent lacks, an earlier step's result that left a named question open, and a doubt already stopping a named action. A checkable fact about a named thing stays observable when the line adds the agent's doubt about that same thing, as 'if the lockfile is stale or you can't tell' does, and so does a judgment of value that an observable kind of work and an explicit grant both bound, as 'if a long check is worth running in the background and the host allows it' does.
criteria.condition: Its condition can't be observed: it names a topic, a need or a feeling with nothing in the work to check, including the agent's own doubt about a quality, such as 'if the skill needs more depth', 'if useful', 'if needed', 'when appropriate' or 'if unsure', so nothing in the work tells the agent it holds. A condition someone else can see, such as a disagreement already raised or a result already returned, is observable.
criteria.work: The condition is observable, but the line doesn't name the different work it causes, or the work is the same with or without it.

condition.finding: Branch condition can't be observed in the work.

work.finding: Branch doesn't name the different work its condition causes.

instructions.task: Does SKILL.md show the all-run spine, from load to completion, in one scan? First identify the job promised by the description and opening model. Then trace its entry/admission or dispatch, the work it calls for, and its returned result, handoff, sufficiency check or stop. This is a spine test, not a workflow-list test: a compact judgment/application route or conditional dispatch to references can satisfy it. In a judgment skill, framing the question, applying the lens and checking or stating the result can be the whole route. A role can admit its commission, dispatch to its supplied phase/procedure and state its handback/completion obligations. Read body plus outline, numbered_first_lines and completion_first_lines as supplementary context; those first lines do not impose a numbering requirement. A formal Done heading and one universally numbered procedure are unnecessary. If the cut hides decisive material, stay uncertain instead of inventing it.

criteria.true: The visible body makes the job's entry-to-result route traceable in one scan, in the form its job needs: ordered steps, a compact judgment/application route, conditional reference dispatch or a mix. A branch may return its specified result or exact gap; an explicit sufficiency/handback check can be completion.
criteria.false: The visible body gives disconnected advice, topic/rule lists or optional references without showing how an entering agent chooses/applies the work and reaches its result or completion boundary. Missing numbering alone is not a failure; a formal process must not be demanded of a compact judgment.

no.finding: Numbered lists hold no workflow, and the all-run spine from load to completion isn't visible.
